liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): Barney pretended to play bass while Phil played behind the rack; fitting for April Fools' Day; Reviewer was astonished when Barney came out to play bass on Iko Iko [1][4][13][15]
- **Rain** (2 reviews): Rain encore was the best part; fans left into a real soaking rain, like a weather report; Rain was huge and renewed the reviewer's love for the song; reviewer says the band had played it just twice [12][17]
- **Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): High-energy Minglewood with great solos and inspired vocals from Bob; Minglewood was the smoking first-set highlight, which is unusual for that song [14][16]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer was overwhelmed enough to sit down during Drums/Space [10]
- **Way to Go Home** (1 review): Reviewer also recommends the Way to Go Home as a highlight of an otherwise sloppy night [11]
- **Wave to the Wind** (1 review): Reviewer describes Wave to the Wind as a train wreck, as usual [11]
- **Liberty** (1 review): First set closed with an upbeat Liberty, one of the new spring 1993 numbers [16]
- Reviewer calls the Days Between worth hearing despite a sloppy show overall [11]
- Reviewer finds the Days Between excellent [13]
- Tight Garcia solo, lots of interplay with Bobby and Phil, and a funky Vince solo; sounds like late-70s JGB [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd93-04-01 t01 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t02 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t03 Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t04 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t05 Desolation Row**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t06 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t07 Eternity**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd93-04-01 t08 Liberty**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-04-01.139690.fob.schoeps.wise.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 155 min [1]
- **gd1993-04-01.150157.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 153 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd93-04-01.sbd.hinko.23822.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 152 min; rated 2.71/5 by 14 [5]
- **gd93-04-01.bk4011.blanchard.17682.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 159 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer had backstage passes and recalls someone whacking the strings, the one detail remembered from the night [9]
- Reviewer hitchhiked from Lake Placid to Nassau for a first show, meeting friends who had come from the Albany shows [10]
- Barney the purple dinosaur appeared on bass, a treat for Phil's kids [10]
- Barney was onstage, but Phil later told the reviewer personally that it was not him in the costume [12]
- Reviewer's car radio antenna was stolen in the parking lot during the show [15]
- When Barney appeared, the crowd stood stunned; one fan joked about a dinosaur supposedly unseen at Hampton [17]
- Reviewer rates it a weak four stars, but strong among spring 1993 shows [13]
- Reviewer saw four of the five Nassau run shows and ranked this the best [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-04-01.139690.fob.schoeps.wise.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise and Scott Clugston; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Jim Wise's FOB Audience DAT > Schoeps CMC6/MK4 (hand-held ORTF) > Sonosax SX-M2 > Dat (Sony D10 Pro/48k); Transfer Info: DAT Master… [1]. Also: Schoeps-based transfer; the stretch from 2:46 through the end of Liberty comes from an AKG source [1]
- **gd1993-04-01.150157.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  May 25, 2020; source: SBD > DAT Master (48k) > Cassette Master (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) [4]
- **gd93-04-01.sbd.hinko.23822.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [5]. Also: Soundboard chain: DSBD to cassette to DAT to CD, then EAC and SHN by Darryl Hinko [5]
- **gd93-04-01.bk4011.blanchard.17682.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Steve Blanchard; source: Audience: B&K 4011's [7]. Also: Audience recording on B&K 4011 mics, placed at the stacks front center; converted from CD by Steve Blanchard [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1993-04-01 Nassau Coliseum, Uniondale, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1993-04-01-nassau-coliseum-uniondale-ny-usa/) [22]
- Fan art by @evevintageshop: [Grateful Dead April Fools 1993 Nassau Coliseum Tie-dye Shirt](https://evevintage.com/product/grateful-dead-april-fools-1993-tie-dye/) [23]
